newsitem.title: USA: Calif. exports to show strong growth in '97-report.
newsitem.headline: Calif. exports to show strong growth in '97-report.

text.p: California's exports are forecast to reach $123 billion in 1997, up from an estimated $108 billion for 1996, according to a report released Tuesday by Bank of America's International Trade Bank.

The state's exports will be concentrated in Pacific Rim countries. Although economic growth in many Asian countries will slow in 1997 because of cyclical factors, California's exports to these markets will remain strong, the report said.

Many Asian countries will proceed with efforts to restructure their economies, resulting in continued import demand for California's high-technology and information-intensive products, the report said.
The expansion in Asia projected for 1997 will offer opportunities for California exporters of all sizes, particularly those that can help meet the region's infrastructure needs, it said.

California's export growth to Mexico and Canada is predicted to outpace the state's overall growth of exports in 1997, the report said, adding that Russia represents a potentially lucrative market for California's exporters.
